translations.title: To Him
translations.text:
No bond remains: everything is broken.
Heaven willed it so: blessed be its will!
I gladly drain the bitter cup;
my soul rests at last and desires nothing.

I loved you; I love you no longer—or so I think.
If I am wrong, may I never see the truth!
Let oblivion swallow so many bitter years;
let my heart breathe again.

You shattered it without pity; my pride
you trampled over and over in your frenzy...
Yet my lips will never breathe a murmur
to accuse you of your tyranny.

As the dread avenger of grave offenses,
you dutifully fulfilled your mission; do you know it?
The irresistible power that laid my strength
prostrate before you was not yours.

God willed it, and so it was: glory to his name!
All is over; I draw breath again.
Angel of vengeance! You are a man now...
I feel neither love nor fear when I behold you.

Your scepter fell, your sword grew dull...
But ah, how sadly I breathe this freedom!
I made a world of you, and now it falls to nothing,
leaving me in deep and boundless solitude.

May you live happily! If someday
you see this farewell I send you forever,
know that in my soul you still have
generous forgiveness and tender affection.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Poland
translations.text:
Free translation of Victor Hugo

Alone at the foot of the tower, where the thunderous voice
of your fatal lord resounds in terror,
whose sinister shadow seems at moments
to mark the stone of the silent threshold;

ready to see your husband turn murderer,
pale, your neck bowed to the ground,
vanquished and chained, you offer yourself to fate,
beautiful, sorrowful Poland, its unhappy victim.

In place of your children, I see your pure hands
clasp the holy crucifix fervently.
The Bashkirs have stained your royal garments
and stamped them with their sandals as they passed!

At intervals words of menace reach you,
and the sound of heavy footsteps is heard;
a saber flashes there, and an iron shackle binds you
to the wall down which your painful tears run.

Unfortunate Poland! I see you lift
your wasted arms and bowed brow,
and turn your tearful, sunken, clouded eyes
toward France with a timid gaze.

A most sorrowful cry escapes your breast:
“O France, my sister!” I hear you repeat.
Anxiously you search the road with your eyes,
and wait, alas, and wait... and see no one come!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Delicate Flower, Which Lives Barely One Dawn...
translations.text:
The delicate flower, which lives barely one dawn,
may leave its scent in the air for a long time...
But alas, the flowers the soul once treasured,
when they die and wither, leave no fragrance behind.

The splendid light of the day's fruitful star
goes out, yet its traces still make a lovely afterglow...
But alas, when the soul's dark night arrives,
what preserves the sacred fire that was its sun?

The string of the harmonious harp, worn thin, breaks,
yet its echo still sends a fleeting vibration through the air...
But all is deep silence, the dread silence of death,
when a loving heart sounds its last, most sorrowful note.

Yet nothing—not night, dawn, or uncertain dusk—
changes the mournful face of the desolate soul.
No twilight, fragrance, or breeze reaches it;
no shadows offer it dreams of peace.

Let gracious spring clothe the fields in flowers;
let summer's sky kiss the harvests gold;
let vine leaves adorn autumn's cheerful face;
let misty winter breathe its icy breath:

always lost and wandering in their barren desert,
always crushed beneath the weight of vile emptiness,
souls in which the fire of love is dead lament.
Nothing fills or enlivens their great solitude.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To France
translations.text:
Let it suffice you, O France, the thunderous glory
with which that man filled all your realms;
let it suffice to see his illustrious name
joined to yours in immortal history.
Let the memory suffice
of those great days
when at his voice you made Europe tremble;
and leave the world that austere tomb
where stern fate keeps
the giant of ambition and pride,
among those barren, lonely rocks,
while the sea, with turbulent lullaby,
breaks its foaming waves at his feet.

Leave him there! Without a retinue, alone,
let the king without a dynasty sleep
on his solitary, cold rock.
Do not bury him in a narrow pantheon
where he would hear the bacchanal din of Paris,
confused with common kings.

Leave him there, for his place is Saint Helena!
The mighty names of Wagram, Austerlitz,
Marengo, and Jena will not return
the silent echoes to disturb the peace
of his rough tomb, where the imperial eagle
casts no shadow with its wings, nor hollow bronze
resounds in all its power to salute it.
Yet there the world beholds him and marvels
at the mystery silently revealed:
for the immense specter,
suspended there between heaven and abyss,
perhaps fulfilling sovereign designs,
is a monument of human history
that gives peoples and tyrants
a lofty lesson, a terrible warning!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Quatrains Written in a Cemetery
translations.text:
Here is the refuge of eternal calm,
where only the drooping willow grows.
Leave me here: my weary soul
longs for the air among the graves.

You who breathe life's flowers,
full of the scents of pleasure and glory,
do not tread this place where you will see
their splendor turned to wretched dross.

But come, all of you who saw fate's angry brow
as you lay in your cradles;
you whose hearts are wounded
and who expect no comfort.

Come too, ardent spirits
who wander restlessly through this world,
whose immense thirst its muddy springs
cannot quench with their meager flow!

You who knew weariness before
the years brought peace and quiet,
come with your consuming dreams!
Come with your sorrowful disillusionments!

Here neither pleasure counts the hours,
fast or slow, nor hope measures them.
Here the turbulent waves break
that the hurricane of passions casts up.

Here, if shadows of doubt disturb you,
stern, steadfast truth keeps watch.
Here eternal, silent peace reigns,
if a weary soul longs for peace.

Those who sleep their deep sleep here
once tossed sleeplessly as we do.
In death's deadly balm they have cooled
their fevered brows.

Let us love, then, our future home,
the only one we have that endures.
For life's happiness is an illusion,
but the peace of death is real!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Elegy I
translations.text:
After the death of my husband

Once more tears, solitude, darkness...
The cherished dream has fled like smoke!
The beloved light that lit my life
was but a flash of lightning.

It shone to reveal the shadows of the past;
it shone to announce the shadows ahead;
it shone only to die... and in dark night
I was left forever.

After long years of bitter storms
I was beginning to enjoy a gentle calm;
but alas, grief left my soul only
to mock it.

So the treacherous beast pretends
to let its hapless prey escape,
and draws back, claws outstretched,
to seize it all the better.

He who yesterday was my support and refuge
today is death's wretched trophy.
For a bridal wreath, Hymen gave me
a withered, sorrowful cypress!

Full of youth, love, and strength,
how vast his future seemed...
But his day ended in the morning:
he belongs to time no more!

Nothing remains to me, O God! My beautiful hope
folds its broken wings and moans.
Today fate seals its decrees;
now they cannot be undone.

Perhaps my poor life will survive
the cruel blow that tears my breast;
but with the remains swallowed by that tomb
my heart sinks too.

Noble and loving soul! Before the throne
of infinite fatherly mercy,
for her who was half your life,
pray, pray for pity!

May a ray of light descend to illumine my soul
in this abyss of profound dread,
until I may leave behind
the world's immense solitude!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To a Firefly
translations.text:
Tell me, mysterious light,
that wanders before my eyes,
awakens my interest
and charms my sleepless hours:

Are you perhaps a lamp
cast down from heaven,
passing as a pilgrim
through this wretched earth?

Are you a spirit or sylph
of our unspoiled homeland,
holding the fiery sap
of its young life within you?

Are you perhaps the wandering soul
of someone dear,
come to ask me for
remembrance and prayers;

or else a shining spark
from the bright wings
with which heavenly hope
sustains the sorrowful?

I do not know; but when you shine
beautifully before my eyes
in the solemn stillness
of tropical nights,

whether, a wandering exhalation,
you cross the clear sphere,
or play like a breeze,
swaying among the reeds;

whether, like a pure diamond,
you set yourself among the palms,
imitating their whisper,
adorning their green with light;

I seem to feel
a strange revelation
of mystical love
between your glow and my soul.

I seem to sense
secret harmonies
between the longing I conceal
and the radiance you give off.

O star or sylph,
soul or spirit, then,
cast brighter sparks
as my voice sings to you!

May the notes of my lyre
and the sparks of your flame
mingle and travel
through mountains and savannas,

and rise to heaven
in the fragrance of the fields,
where kindred stars
call them to themselves,

where he sets his throne
who understands and weighs
the essence of every light,
the cause of every longing!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Revenge
translations.text:
You want to wash away
with wine's dulling haze
the bitterness of oblivion I left upon your lips;
you are the dust cloud in my path,
and I the rock amid your dizzying turns.

It is useless for you to follow my fate
with the sarcasm your foot stirs up.
I was the whirlwind that struck your pride,
and you the flood that burst its banks.

And so, to drown your ambitions,
I will lash you with laughter in my songs,
and yoke you like a slave to my tracks.

While a hundred women's eyes
will offer you, amid lustful pleasures,
my own image distorted within them.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Canto XXXV: Imitation
translations.text:
Far from my own branch,
poor delicate leaf,
where are you going? From the beech
where I was born, the wind tore me away.

It comes again and carries me
from forest to countryside,
from valley to mountain.

With it, forever,
I wander, and know nothing else.

I go where all things go,
where, by nature,
the rose leaf goes
and the laurel leaf.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
